text:
Dinesh Rao: FYI — flipped FP8 for the L40S/H100 canary last night. Baseline throughput looks fine for short contexts but we're seeing a big degradation for long-context user traces (>6k). 95/99 latencies spike and some requests hit retry/backpressure. :eyes:

Eva Morris: ugh. did we change the kernel selector policy or just the quantization profile?

Dinesh Rao: only turned on the fp8 kernels + transformer-engine flags we landed. selector is still 'auto' but candidate ordering changed because fp8 kernels report lower estimated cycles.

perf-bot: Perf report uploaded: https://dash.internal/runs/2491112222 (flamegraphs + heatmaps). Hotspots: attention-mutator, kv-merge path, and the cross-attn matmul_stable_fp8 kernel.

Alice K: Can you paste a short sample of the flamegraph output? I want to check fusion vs non-fusion paths.

Dinesh Rao: snippet from the profile: 
```
HOT: matmul_stable_fp8 (45%)
HOT: kv_cache_apply (22%)
HOT: tensor_fuse (12%)
HOT: fallback_int8_shim (7%)
```
Looks like we hit a fallback shim path intermittently which serializes some kernels.

Ben Ortiz: That fallback shim rings alarm bells. Could be numerical stability detection in the fp8 kernels triggering a slow path. Did the calibration change scale/bias thresholds?

Dinesh Rao: calibration unchanged for this rollout. But transformer-engine now uses per-tensor scale clipping. guessing dynamic range on some heads causes occasional clamp + dequantize loop.

Carla Nguyen: Also saw a lot more small microbatches in the traces — upstream batching heuristic seems to be breaking on these traces (many congested requests). microbatch count jumps from 1->12 quickly which amplifies the evict-serialize pattern. We should confirm if the batching window / max_wait got tweaked.

Eva Morris: Good call. @Ben can you check the batching config in canary? I rolled back a tweak yesterday but not this one.

Ben Ortiz: Checking... config shows batch_window_ms=6 (was 10), max_batch_tokens=131072 (unchanged), prefer_fused_ops=true. That batch_window change was to reduce latency for short requests but may be fragmenting attention windows for long contexts.

Alice K: If batch_window_ms is too small we get more kernel switches and less steady-state occupancy on the GPU. For FP8 especially, kernel launch overhead + dequantize path is relatively sensitive. Suggest bumping to 12ms in canary to repro.

perf-bot: Quick telemetry excerpt (p50/p95/p99 across canary): 
```
p50: 82ms, p95: 230ms, p99: 1420ms (long ctx traces)
GPU occupancy: median 65% but 99th 18% during spikes
kernel_switch_count: +3.6x vs baseline
fp8_fallback_rate: 6.7% of requests
kv_cache_miss_rate: +1.8% (long ctx)
```

Carla Nguyen: kv_cache_miss increase is interesting — maybe layout differences for fp8 tensors changed eviction heuristics. Are we storing cache in fp32 or compacted? I thought we keep kv cache in fp16 to avoid precision loss.

Dinesh Rao: KV cache is stored in fp16. The fp8 kernels currently do on-the-fly quant for attention inputs then dequantize back for the cache write. That path wasn't fully optimized and appears to conflict with the eviction fast-path, causing temporary stalls.

Ben Ortiz: Two actionable experiments: 1) force selector to prefer fp16 attention kernels (no fp8) to see if throughput returns. 2) increase batch_window_ms to 12-15 to reduce fragmentation.

Alice K: Also add an A/B with transformer-engine flag "use_cuda_graphs=false" — we suspect cuda-graph capture + fp8 reorder is causing rare launch reorder that misses fused kernels. If disabling cuda graphs solves it, we can narrow root cause.

Eva Morris: I'll run the A/B now on a subset (10% traffic). Dinesh, can you attach the exact canary config?

Dinesh Rao: Canary config: 
```
model: gptj-xxl-fp8
kernel_selector: auto
batch_window_ms: 6
prefer_fused_ops: true
transformer_engine: { fp8_enabled: true, use_cuda_graphs: true, per_tensor_clamp: true }
kv_cache_layout: fp16
```

Dinesh Rao: Also attaching a short repro script we used locally that shows the fallback flip: 
```
# repro client
for i in seq 1 200; do 
  curl -s -X POST $CANARY_URL -d @long_trace.json; 
  sleep 0.05; 
done
```

Carla Nguyen: When you run that locally with nvprof are you seeing any memcpy spikes near the kv write? That would confirm the dequantize -> memcpy -> write pattern.

Dinesh Rao: Yes — nvprof shows a memcpy after matmul_stable_fp8 for the fallback cases. That line is absent when we force fp16 kernels.

Ben Ortiz: Ok plan of attack: 
- Roll an A/B: A = force fp16 kernels, B = current fp8 config but batch_window_ms=12, C = current config + use_cuda_graphs=false (three arms, 5/45/50 split).
- Add temporary telemetry: kernel_switch_count, fp8_fallback_rate, memcpy-after-attn flag.
- Throttle canary to 3k qps for initial run.

Alice K: I'll add a quick selector override in runtime so we can flip without redeploy. Also push a micro-optimization to avoid dequantize memcpy if we detect cache will be written to fp16 directly (skip memcopy).

perf-bot: Action items created: RD-1402 (A/B rollout), RD-1403 (telemetry hooks), RD-1404 (selector override).

Eva Morris: Starting A/B now. I'll post results in this thread in ~30m. :thumbsup: 

Dinesh Rao: Thanks — if anyone wants to look at the raw flamegraphs I uploaded a tarball to /mnt/perf/2491112222/flame.tar.zst. Also saving the repro traces under /mnt/repro/2491112222/

Ben Ortiz: One more note — if fp8 fallback is nondeterministic we might be hitting race between the kernel's stability check and the quant table update. I'll instrument kernel to log fallback reason in debug builds.

Carla Nguyen: Logging fallback reasons will help correlate with kv cache misses. Good call.

Eva Morris: A/B is live. early numbers: arm A (fp16 forced) p99 for long ctx dropped to ~320ms; arm B (larger window) p99 ~580ms; arm C (no cuda graphs) p99 ~430ms. Seems forcing fp16 fixes majority of spike. More data after 30m.

Dinesh Rao: That's huge — so FP8 baseline path seems legit but fallback/interaction with batching/kernel capture causes tail issues. We should pause broad rollout until we ship the dequantize fast-path and fallback logging.

Alice K: Agreed. I'll prepare a revert plan and patch to skip the memcpy if cache target width==fp16. Expect PR by EOD.

Ben Ortiz: I'll keep digging into selector heuristics too. Might need to add a stability penalty in auto-selector for fp8 on H100 with long contexts.

Dinesh Rao: Thanks team. I'll update RD-1402 with the final numbers and mark canary paused for wider rollout.

perf-bot: Thread pinned to eng-runtime for 48h."
